marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q001.takeaway: The urogenital ridge is derived from intermediate mesoderm and separates into a medial genital ridge and lateral nephrogenic cord.
marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q001.displayText: The urogenital ridge develops from intermediate mesoderm, which forms a longitudinal bulge on the posterior abdominal wall after formation of the peritoneal cavity. Its medial component is the genital ridge, which contributes to the genital system, while its lateral component is the nephrogenic cord, which contributes to the urinary system.

rationales.a: Paraxial mesoderm forms somites and their derivatives; it does not form the urogenital ridge.
rationales.c: Lateral plate mesoderm contributes to body-wall and visceral mesodermal structures, not the urogenital ridge.
rationales.d: Extraembryonic mesoderm lies outside the embryo proper and is not the source of the urogenital ridge.

marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q002.takeaway: Metanephric blastema forms the nephron excretory segments, whereas the ureteric bud forms the collecting system.
marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q002.displayText: The proximal convoluted tubule develops from the metanephric blastema. The metanephric blastema forms Bowman's capsule, proximal convoluted tubule, loop of Henle and distal convoluted tubule—the excretory portion of the definitive kidney. In contrast, the ureteric bud, an outgrowth of the mesonephric duct, forms the collecting ducts, calyces, renal pelvis and ureter. Glomerular capillaries arise from angiogenic mesenchyme.

rationales.a: The mesonephric duct gives rise to the ureteric bud but does not directly form the proximal convoluted tubule.
rationales.c: Mesonephric tubules belong to the transient mesonephric kidney and are not the source of definitive proximal convoluted tubules.
rationales.d: The ureteric bud forms the collecting system, whereas the proximal convoluted tubule is a metanephric-blastema derivative.

marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q003.takeaway: The ureteric bud sprouts from the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct and forms the ureter plus the collecting system of the kidney.
marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q003.displayText: The ureteric bud develops as an outgrowth of the mesonephric duct (Wolffian duct). Its tip enters the metanephric blastema and undergoes branching to form the collecting ducts, renal papillae, minor and major calyces, renal pelvis and ureter. The surrounding metanephric blastema instead forms Bowman's capsule, proximal convoluted tubule, loop of Henle and distal convoluted tubule.

rationales.b: There is no metanephric duct that gives rise to the ureteric bud; the bud arises from the mesonephric duct.
rationales.c: The paramesonephric (Müllerian) duct forms major female reproductive-tract derivatives, not the ureteric bud.
rationales.d: A separate 'ureter duct' is not the embryologic source; the ureter itself is a derivative of the ureteric bud.

marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q004.takeaway: The source nephron-development sequence is blastema stage → vesicle stage → comma-shaped stage → S-shaped stage, corresponding to reconstructed labels 1-4-2-3 (option C).
marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q004.displayText: The printed source explanation gives the developmental sequence as blastema stage → vesicle stage → comma-shaped (C-shaped) stage → S-shaped stage. The ureteric-bud ampulla induces adjacent metanephric mesenchyme, which epithelializes into a renal vesicle and develops through comma-shaped and S-shaped stages. The original question page omits its numbered stage definitions. A contextual reconstruction uses this explicit source sequence and printed key C (1-4-2-3): 1 = blastema stage, 2 = comma-shaped stage, 3 = S-shaped stage, and 4 = vesicle stage. These labels are inferred from the source explanation and key, rather than transcribed from a visible original list. Thus the restored stages give 1-4-2-3. The source sequence includes the comma-shaped stage; it does not substitute a definitive nephron as the fourth listed stage.
emphasis: blastema stage → vesicle stage → comma-shaped (C-shaped) stage → S-shaped stage

rationales.a: Under the reconstructed legend, 1-2-3-4 puts the vesicle stage last, although vesicle formation precedes comma-shaped and S-shaped stages.
rationales.b: Under the reconstructed legend, 4-3-2-1 starts with the vesicle stage and ends with blastema, reversing the developmental direction.
rationales.d: Under the reconstructed legend, 1-4-3-2 places the S-shaped stage before the comma-shaped stage; comma-shaped development precedes the S-shaped stage.
